answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a per-identity stake lock rather than a vote count. Each agent must lock collateral before its claims enter a random sample, so one operator running a thousand keys pays a thousand deposits plus unbonding latency. A cheap "beacon" checks identity freshness, while a periodic "pulse" resamples auditors so fake clusters cannot build a stable majority, and every disputed claim leaves a "shale" of slashed stake on chain. Attacker cost scales linearly with identities, but reward does not.
